title: Finite Kummer boundary from normalized Chern comparisons
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and T a scheme. For any existing Chern data c [def-sp-tower-class-chern] satisfying the three equations c.Normalized, the resulting actual firstChern arrows satisfy FiniteChernNormalization [def-sp-tower-class-finite]. For every line bundle and positive quotient level the evaluated, forgotten coefficient-linear arrow, precomposed with finiteQuotient, equals the evaluated positive Kummer connecting composite followed by finiteRootMap, with the exact endpoint transports recorded by finiteBoundaryEquality. No new Chern data are constructed.

proof.text: Expand firstChernR as the inverse source comparison followed by reduction of lineBundleClass and the target comparison. Apply the reduction adjunction Hom bijection. Naturality in lineBundleClass, sourceNormalization and targetNormalization identify its composite with the integer generator with the positive Kummer composite. The specified shift-addition comparison keeps its sign.

source.place: clause (2), evaluation gives the finite Kummer first Chern class; expanded SmoothPurityTowerClasses proof, steps 5--8

proof.text: For scalar extension, choose a K-flat representative and apply the representative transpose identity of ScalarData there. Naturality of the universal counit passes this equality through the resolution isomorphism to the original object; no K-flatness of an arbitrary root module concentrated in degree zero is assumed. Apply the scalar unitNormalization equation. The ordinary unit sends z to one tensor z. The universal scalar counit is exactly the lineComparison appearing in firstChern, including its shift comparison, so the resulting equality uses the actual Chern morphism.

source.place: clause (2), evaluation gives the finite Kummer first Chern class; expanded SmoothPurityTowerClasses proof, steps 5--8

proof.text: Apply exact evaluation and finite forgetting, keeping their canonical single and shift comparisons. Exact functors preserve the connecting morphism of the Kummer short exact sequence. The integer map is finiteQuotient by uniqueness on constant integer sections, and the root map is finiteRootMap by uniqueness on z mapping to one tensor z. The pure-tensor equation for lineEvaluation identifies the target comparison. These equalities, with the two endpoint-transport witnesses, are precisely finiteBoundaryEquality for each line bundle and level.
